submission.natural_language_explanation: The pole is a sparse detector of an explicit numeric quantity in running prose: it peaks on the token that carries the number - a digit of a numeral, a '%' sign, or a magnitude/scale word (hundred, hundreds, thousand, thousands, million, millions, billion, lakh, percent, decade, hour) - when the number states a value on an established scale, such as an age or age bracket ('men aged 25', 'from 15 to 99'), a version or model number ('iOS 6', 'IE8', 'Excel 2007', 'gcc 4.4'), a share ('90% of the media') or a duration ('20 years', '30 minutes'). Within a numeral the strength sits on the digit that continues or closes the number rather than the first one ('25' fires at the '5', '90%' at '0' and '%'), and the pole is near zero on ordinary words, on the first digit of a bare object count ('25 engineers', '25 chairs') and on numerals frozen into identifiers or notation (URLs, file paths, parentheses, room and phone numbers, citation dates, code constants); its positive pole is a separate literal-'+' detector.

Q:

Corona sdk Get Sim Card Details

I'm creating an Application using Corona sdk with Lua Language, can anyone help me with getting Sim Card details such as, mobile Number, pin no .. etc
Thank you

A:

Corona provides system.getInfo() for getting device-specific information. I dont think you can find the mobile Number, but there is some info you can get.
You can get more details in the docs
You probably will find deviceID useful:

On iOS, "deviceID" returns a "unique" id for the device. Per Apple's policies, on iOS 6 and later, "deviceID" returns a MD5 hash of the device's "identifierForVendor" (see below); on iOS 5 it returns a MD5 of a GUID (Globally Unique Identifier) that is unique for each app install.
On Android, if your app uses the "android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE" permission, the following will be returned:

IMEI for GSM phones.
MEID or ESN for CDMA phones.
The operating system's unique ID for devices that are not phones.

If your Android app does not use the "android.permission.READ_PHONE_STATE" permission, then the operating system's unique ID will be returned for all devices. Note that the operating system's unique ID may change after re-installing the operating system on the device.

As the wet shaving world continues to grow and flourish, new artisans begin to jump on the scene: artisans who not only realize the benefit of traditional wet shaving, but spend careful time and research dedicated to providing products that help us to slow down, smell the roses, and enjoy a well-crafted shave. Since this oftentimes becomes a hobby and - for many - a community, we thought it’d be fun to engage with some of our recent artisans and ask them a few questions so you can get to know them better, and buy with confidence!

Cooper & French: Minnesota-based artisans Richard and Stephanie have been making leaps and bounds on the wet shaving subreddit communities as of late, with a great selection of slick shaving soaps and comforting aftershave balms, all at a great pricepoint!

1. How did you get into wet shaving?

I was very unhappy with using canned foam and cartridge razors, both in terms of performance and cost for a long time. 20 years ago I had become so frustrated that I grew a full beard. Eight or nine years ago I flirted with a straight razor, but fell victim to my own ignorance and soon gave it up. Three years ago I made another run at it with similar results; on a whim I googled safety razors and soon fell down the proverbial rabbit hole of wet shaving.

2. What is your hardware (brush/razor/blade) of choice?

I have nine safety razors in my medicine cabinet! My Gillette Super Speed Red Tip and Slim get the most love. I still use the same 24mm synthetic brush I bought new three years ago. I have a large stack of sample blades thanks to a very generous Secret Santa last year, which has afforded me opportunities to try many blades. I find the Gillette Silver Blue razor blade consistently gives a great shave in a variety of razors.

3. What are your favorite pastimes and/or hobbies?

I collect and refurbish antique woodworking tools (time and motivation permitting). A finely tuned 100 year old hand plane is a thing of beauty to use.

4. Are there any influences or interesting backgrounds on any scents of yours?

My very first scent, Fresh Start, is my own essential oil creation. Born of the materials I had on hand and a half baked idea. It didn't really turn out how I had imagined it would. I very nearly tossed out the samples I had blended. It was my wife who prompted me to try it in a test batch.

Gerda Gilboe (5 July 1914 – 11 April 2009) was a Danish actress and singer. She appeared in 18 films between 1943 and 2003.

Life 
Gilboe was born in 1914. She was the daughter of a blacksmith, Gilboe started her career in musical theatre and operas in Aarhus before she moved to Copenhagen to work at different theatres. Her national breakthrough came, when she  accepted the role as Eliza in My Fair Lady at Falkoner Teatret at short notice in 1960. Although she was then in her mid-40s and had only five days to learn the part, the production was a huge success.

In the following years she took on more and more non-singing roles, and besides her theatre career she took a degree in rhetoric. Later in her life she started teaching rhetoric and drama. She appeared in several films, receiving particular acclaim for her appearance as Esther in Carlo & Esther, a 1994 film. She plays a woman in her 70s who catches the attention of Carlo who has a wife with Alzheimer's disease. Rides on his motorbike lead to an affair.

Death 
Gilboe died on 11 April 2009 at an actors' home in Copenhagen, aged 94.

Why was Mundungus banned from the Hog's Head?

In Order of the Phoenix while the trio were in the Hogs Head for the first time plotting the start of Dumbledore's Army, it transpires that ol' Dung was lurking in the pub in a disguise, having been banned 20 years previously according to Sirius. 
Firstly, why was he banned? this could possibly be the tight spot that Albus had helped Dung with in the first place that made him loyal to Albus.  
And secondly, how is it that he is then speaking to Aberforth in Halfblood Prince? (assuming the ban was for something rather unforgivable, 20 years is a long time?) 
They both could have been in the Order by then, but unlikely given Aberforth's attitude in Deathly Hallows once the trio arrive in Hogsmeade looking for the tiara.  We learn now that a lot of trafficking goes on through the Hogs Head so maybe Dung was trading with Aberforth, Sirius' mirror and various other Black artifacts, he just was not allowed in the pub.

why was he banned?

Q:

Download OS X App Store updates to update multiple Macs

I have two MacBook Airs, but I have very limited bandwidth. I would prefer to download updates once and then copy them onto all the other MacBook Airs. How can I download App Store updates once to update multiple Macs?

A:

There are two types of update.
OS X software updates are updates for the OS and OS components (e.g. iTunes). These used to be delivered through a separate software update app, but since the introduction of the Mac App Store, the OS X updates have been combined with Mac App Store updates in the Updates tab of the Mac App Store. However, the CLI tool remains, giving you more flexibility in Terminal and allow the downloading of updates without installing them, perfect for copying to other machines before the installation takes place.
You can download OS X updates without installing them (which would automatically remove them) so you can copy them, using the following command:
softwareupdate -dav

The 10.9.4 update is distributed externally, outside of the Mac App Store; the Mac App Store just provides the UI for the installation process.
Conversely, for Mac App Store apps, you need OS X Server's Caching service, as the apps are 'non-transferrable' and the app receipt must match the Apple ID that downloaded the app for the app to be updated in the future. However, if you're using the same Apple ID, or don't care about updating the app from the second machine, update the app normally then copy the .app bundle from /Applications to the other Macs as necessary.

adversarial_test_results.prompt:
Every autumn the Harbor Point library association sends a letter to its members, and this year the letter was longer than usual. The building on Wharf Street has stood since the fishing boom, when the town's population was small enough that a single librarian could shelve the entire collection in an afternoon. Over the following years the collection grew, the roof sagged, and the reading room was quietly converted into a storage closet for donated paperbacks.

When the association finally commissioned a survey of the structure, the report was blunt. The foundation was sound, but the wiring predated modern codes, the windows leaked, and the children's section had no ventilation at all. Volunteers spent a winter cataloguing every damaged title, taping spines and marking water stains with coloured slips of paper, while the board argued about budgets in the basement meeting room.

The first appeal went out in the spring and raised far less than anyone hoped. A retired teacher organized a used-book sale on the lawn, which brought in enough for new shelving but nothing for the roof. A local contractor offered to donate labour if the association could cover materials, and a grant application was submitted, rejected, rewritten and submitted again. Supporters wrote letters to the county paper, and one of them, a former deckhand, recalled borrowing sea stories from the library as a boy and reading them by the light of a kerosene lamp.

By midsummer the campaign had acquired a momentum of its own. Schoolchildren painted a mural on the plywood covering the broken window, the Rotary club pledged a matching gift, and a benefit concert at the bandstand drew a crowd that spilled onto the grass. The board hired an architect who specialized in small civic buildings and asked her to keep the original reading room intact, with its tall windows facing the water, while adding a wing for computers and a proper children's area.

Construction began in the fall and ran through a wet winter. The crew worked around the association's monthly meetings, and the librarian moved the surviving collection into temporary trailers behind the parking lot. There were delays: a shipment of timber arrived warped, the heating contractor quit midway through the job, and a storm flooded the excavation. Each setback produced another round of letters, phone calls and, occasionally, a small emergency appeal that the members answered with remarkable speed.

The renovated building reopened on a Saturday morning with a ribbon cutting, a table of coffee cakes, and a speech that went on longer than the microphone battery lasted. The reading room looked much as it had before, except that the windows no longer leaked and the shelves were no longer crowded with paperbacks nobody wanted. Children ran through the new wing and discovered the computers, and the librarian, who had spent two years working out of a trailer, sat down at her old desk and cried a little.

The renovated wing now holds 220 seats, and 78% of the project's funding came from private donors.

explanation_scores.explanation: The pole is a sparse detector of an explicit numeric quantity in running prose: it peaks on the token that carries the number - a digit of a numeral, a '%' sign, or a magnitude/scale word (hundred, hundreds, thousand, thousands, million, millions, billion, lakh, percent, decade, hour) - when the number states a value on an established scale, such as an age or age bracket ('men aged 25', 'from 15 to 99'), a version or model number ('iOS 6', 'IE8', 'Excel 2007', 'gcc 4.4'), a share ('90% of the media') or a duration ('20 years', '30 minutes'). Within a numeral the strength sits on the digit that continues or closes the number rather than the first one ('25' fires at the '5', '90%' at '0' and '%'), and the pole is near zero on ordinary words, on the first digit of a bare object count ('25 engineers', '25 chairs') and on numerals frozen into identifiers or notation (URLs, file paths, parentheses, room and phone numbers, citation dates, code constants); its positive pole is a separate literal-'+' detector.
